text: Imagine having a meltdown to your husband about how bad your day at work was and instead of telling you to quit your job, take his credit card, buy yourself something nice, and that you're just a girl and shouldn't have to work, he says, I'm sorry, I hope tomorrow is a better day. Imagine being an adult, having accountability, and being able to handle a normal bad day. Work gets stressful, life gets messy. That's part of being a grown human. But if your reaction is, my husband should fix it, tell me to quit my job, hand me his credit card, and remind me I'm just a girl who shouldn't work, then you are not looking for a partnership, you are looking for a sugar daddy. The wild part is she frames this like her husband did something wrong, he listened to her, validated her feelings, wished her a better day. That's what a supportive partner does. But no, she wanted a fantasy sequence, she wanted the royal treatment, the you are just a girl, don't work line. Basically, she expected her husband to pay her way out of her emotions. And guys, here's the truth you need to see. This mindset is becoming alarmingly common. Some women don't want a relationship, they want a financial safety net with a pulse. They want a man who absorbs their stress, funds their coping mechanisms, and shields them from the basic responsibilities of adulthood. Here's the truth, healthy relationships don't work like that. A partner is someone who listens to you, supports you, communicates with you, and works with you. Guys, pick women who want to build a life with you, not be carried through one. Women who appreciate your effort and can reciprocate it.
